title: Posted Schedule: The Grade Allowance on Damage Struck on a Settlement Statement
content:
The grade allowance on damage under Grain Marketing Contracts is struck from the worst damage reading taken on every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition, since a settlement carries the grade of the poorest grain it draws on, and the allowance is the rate of the lowest band whose ceiling the reading does not exceed. Where the allowance arises it is struck on the bushels the statement settles.

| Worst damage reading on every load standing against the contract | Allowance |
|---|---|
| Above 15.0 percent | 0.14 per bushel |
| Above 10.0 percent and at or below 15.0 percent | 0.075 per bushel |
| Above 5.0 percent and at or below 10.0 percent | 0.03 per bushel |
| At or below 5.0 percent | none |

## Which readings are looked at

Every load standing against the contract is read, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer are both read, and the worst reading among them governs.

## The ceilings read at their edges

A reading of exactly 5.0 percent is at the free ceiling and takes nothing. A reading of 5.1 percent is above it and takes 0.03. A reading of exactly 10.0 percent is at the middle ceiling and still takes 0.03; 10.1 percent takes 0.075. A reading of exactly 15.0 percent takes 0.075; 15.1 percent takes 0.14.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A hypothetical statement settles 8,000 bushels, and the worst damage reading on the loads standing against the contract is 12.4 percent. That reading is above the middle ceiling and at or below the upper ceiling, so the allowance is 0.075 per bushel, being 600.00 struck on the bushels the statement settles. Had the worst reading been 4.8 percent, no allowance would be struck at all.
